stem.en: Suppose all four hornbill species are seen in a forest this year, while the old trees they nest in are being lost. Why is the full list not enough to show that the birds are safe?

text.en: A species list can never be correct, as birds move between forests.

feedback.en: A list can be correct. It still cannot show what the birds need.

text.en: Hornbills can raise their young anywhere, so old trees do not matter.

feedback.en: Hornbills nest only in large, old trees with suitable cavities.

text.en: It shows who is here now, not whether what they need will last.

feedback.en: Right. A species can be present while what it depends on is being lost.

text.en: Once nest trees are lost, the species has already died out everywhere.

feedback.en: The birds in this case are still present. The worry is about what comes next.

explanation.en: A list shows who is present today. Young hornbills need cavities in old trees, so losing the trees can harm the next generation while adults are still seen.

hints.en: Separate "is the species here now" from "will what it needs still be here".
